verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              धिगस्तु क्षत्तारमिति ब्रुवाणो दर्पेण मत्तो धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रः। अवैक्षत प्रातिकामीं सभायामुवाच चैनं परमार्यमध्ये॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Intoxicated with pride, the son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana) spoke. “Fie on Khattwa.” Casting his eye on the Pratikamin, he spoke thus in the Sabha and in the midst of (all) the revered elders.
verses.bhavadeepa: अन्तो नाशकरः ॥१२॥

verses.sanskrit:
दुर्योधन उवाच।
              प्रातिकामिन्द्रौपदीमानयस्व न ते भयं विद्यते पाण्डवेभ्यः। क्षत्ता ह्ययं विवदत्येव भीतो न चास्माकं वृद्धिकामः सदैव॥२॥
verses.english: Duryodhana said Go, Pratikamin and bring Draupadi here. You have no fear from the Pandavas. It is only Khattwa (Vidura) who savers in fear. He never wishes for our prosperity.
verses.bhavadeepa: धिगस्त्विति । अधिब्रुवाण इति पाठे इति शब्दाध्याहारः। अधिकं निर्मर्यादं ब्रुवाण इत्यर्थः । प्रातिकामीशब्द ईकारान्त इन्नन्तश्च ॥१॥

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एवमुक्तः प्रातिकामी स सूतः प्रायाच्छीघ्रं राजवचो निशम्य। प्रविश्य च श्वेव हि सिंहगेष्ठं समासदन्महिषीं पाण्डवानाम्॥३॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having been thus commanded and having heard the words of the king, the Pratikamin, the man of the Suta caste, went with (great haste). As a dog enters a lion's den, he (entered the house) and came to the queen of the Pandavas.
verses.bhavadeepa: विवदति विपरीतं वदति ॥२॥

verses.sanskrit: प्रातिकाम्युवाच। युधिष्ठिरो द्यूतमदेन मत्तो दुर्योधनो द्रौपदि त्वामजैषीत्। सा त्वं प्रपद्यस्व धृतराष्ट्रस्य वेश्म नयामि त्वां कर्मणि याज्ञसेनि॥४॥
verses.english: Pratikamin said O Draupadi, Yudhisthira having been intoxicated with dice you have been won by Duryodhana. Therefore, O Yajnaseni, come now to the house of Dhritarashtra. I shall ' menial work.
verses.bhavadeepa: सिंहगोष्ठं सिंहस्थानम् ॥३॥

verses.sanskrit: द्रौपद्युवाच। कथं त्वेवं वदसि प्रातिकामिको हि दीव्येद्भार्यया राजपुत्रः। मूढो राजा द्यूतमदेन मत्तो ह्यभून्नान्यत्कैतवमस्य किञ्चित्॥५॥
verses.english: Duryodhana said O Pratikamin, why do you say so? Is there any prince who plays staking his (own) wife? The king was certainly intoxicated with dice, or else could he not find any other object or stake?

verses.sanskrit: प्रातिकाम्युवाच। यदा नाभूत्कैतवमन्यदस्य तदाऽदेवीत्पाण्डवोऽजातशत्रुः। न्यस्ताः पूर्वं भ्रातरस्तेन राज्ञा स्वयं चात्मा त्वमथो राजपुत्रि॥६॥
verses.english: Pratikamin said When he had nothing else to stake, it was then that Ajatasatru (Yudhisthira), the son of Pandu, staked you. The king had first staked his brothers, then himself, and then, O princess, he staked you.
verses.bhavadeepa: कैतवं कितवेभ्यो देयं धनम् ॥५॥

verses.sanskrit: द्रौपद्युवाच। गच्छ त्वं कितवं गत्वा सभायां पृच्छ सूतज। किं तु पूर्वं पराजैषीरात्मानमथवा नु माम्॥७॥
verses.english: Draupadi said O son of Suta, go (back) to the Sabha and ask that gambler (Yudhisthira) whom he lost first, himself or me.

verses.sanskrit: एतज्ज्ञात्वा समागच्छ ततो मां नयं सूतज। ज्ञात्वा चिकीर्षितमहं राज्ञो यास्यामि दुःखिता॥८॥
verses.english: Ascertaining. this, O son of Suta, come here and then take me with you. Knowing the desire of the king (Yudhisthira), I shall go with a sorrowful heart.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              सभां गत्वा स चोवाच द्रौपद्यास्तद्वचस्तदा। युधिष्ठिरं नरेन्द्राणां मध्ये स्थितमिदं वचः॥९॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having returned to the Sabha, he (Pratikamin) told all present there the words of Draupadi. He spoke these words to Yudhisthira sitting in the midst of the kings.

verses.sanskrit: कस्येशो नः पराजैषीरिति त्वामाह द्रौपदी। किं नु पूर्वं पराजैषीरात्मानमथवापि माम्॥१०॥
verses.english: Pratikamin said Draupadi has asked you, "Whose lord were you at the time when you lost me in play? Did you lose yourself first or me?

verses.sanskrit: युधिष्ठिरस्तु निश्चेता गतसत्व इवाभवत्। न तं सूतं प्रत्युवाच वचनं साध्वसाधु वा॥११॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Yudhishthira sat like one demented and deprived of reason. He did not five any reply to the Suta, good or ill.

verses.sanskrit:
दुर्योधन उवाच।
              इहैवागत्य पाञ्चाली प्रश्नमेनं प्रभाषताम्। इहैव सर्वे शृण्वन्तु तस्याश्चैतस्य यद्वचः॥१२॥
verses.english: Duryodhana said Let the princess of Panchala come here and put her question. Let every one here in this Sabha hear the worlds that pass between them (her and Yudhisthira).

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              स गत्वा राजभवनं दुर्योधनवशानुगः। उवाच द्रौपदीं सूतः प्रातिकामी व्यथन्निव॥१३॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Going back to the palace, himself much distressed, the Suta, Pratikamin obedient to the command of Duryodhana, spoke thus to Draupadi.

verses.sanskrit: प्रातिकाम्युवाच। सभ्यास्त्वमी राजपुत्र्याह्वयन्ति मन्ये प्राप्तः संशयः कौरवाणाम्। न वै समृद्दिं पालयते लघीयान् यस्त्वां सभां नेष्यति राजपुत्रि॥१४॥
verses.english: Pratikamin said O princess, those that are in the assembly are summoning you. It seems the destruction of the Kurus is near at hand. O princess, when the weak-brained (Duryodhana) is for taking you before the assembly, he will no longer be able to protect his prosperity.

verses.sanskrit: द्रौपद्युवाच। एवं नूनं व्यदधात्संविधाता स्पर्शावुभौ स्पृशतो वृद्धबालौ। धर्मं त्वेकं परमं प्राह लोके स नः शमं धास्यति गोप्यमानः॥१५॥
verses.english: Draupadi said The great ordainer of the world has ordained this. Happiness and misery come to both the old and the young (the wise and the unwise). Dharma has been said to be the highest object in the world. If cherished, it certainly pours blessings on us.
verses.bhavadeepa: लघीयान् नीचतरः ॥१४॥

verses.sanskrit: सोऽयं धर्मो मात्यगात्कौरवान्वै सभ्यान्गत्वा पृच्छ धर्म्यं वचो मे। ते मां ब्रूयुर्निश्चितं तत्करिष्ये धर्मात्मानो नीतिमन्तो वरिष्ठाः॥१६॥
verses.english: Let not Dharma now abandon the Kurus. Going back to the Sabha, speak these my words conformable to virtue and morality. I am ready to do what those virtuous-minded elder conversant with the precepts of morality, definitely tell me (to do).
verses.bhavadeepa: संविधाता ईश्वरः । स्पर्शौ सुखदुःखे वृद्धबालौ पाण्डितमूर्खौ स्पृशतः प्राप्नुतः शमं स्वास्थ्यम् । धास्यति करिष्यति गोप्यमानः रक्ष्यमाणः ॥१५॥

verses.sanskrit: श्रुत्वा सूतस्तद्वचो याज्ञसेन्याः सभां गत्वा प्राह वाक्यं तदानीम्। अधोमुखास्ते न च किञ्चिदूचुर्निर्बन्धं तं धार्तराष्ट्रस्य बुद्ध्वा॥१७॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having heard these words of Yajnaseni (Draupadi), the Suta returned to the Sabha and repeated her words. But all sat with downcast faces, knowing the eagerness and resolution of the son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana).

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              युधिष्ठिरस्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा दुर्योधनचिकीर्षितम्। द्रौपद्याः संमतं दूतं प्राहिणोद्भरतर्षभ॥१८॥
verses.english: O best of the Bharata race, having heard of the intentions of Duryodhana, Yudhisthira sent a trusted messenger to Draupadi,

verses.sanskrit: एकवस्त्रा त्वधोनीवो रोदमाना रजस्वला। सभामागम्य पाञ्चालि श्वशुरस्याग्रतो भव॥१९॥
verses.english: (Saying) "Panchali should appear before her father-in-law by coming to the Sabha, though she is weeping and attired in one piece of cloth with her naval exposed in consequence of her season having came.”

verses.sanskrit: अथ त्वामागतां दृष्ट्वा राजपुत्रीं सभां तदा। सभ्याः सर्वे विनिन्देरन्मनोर्भिर्धृतराष्ट्रजम्॥२०॥
verses.english: O king, having gone to Krishna's (Draupadi's) house in great speed, the intelligent (messenger) informed her of the intentions of Dharmaraja (Yudhisthira).

verses.sanskrit: स गत्वा त्वरितं दूतः कृष्णाया भवनं नृप। न्यवेदयन्मतं धीमान्धर्मराजस्य निश्चितम्॥२१॥
verses.english: The illustrious Pandavas, distressed and sorrowful and bound by promise, could not settle what they should do.

verses.sanskrit: पाण्डवाश्च महात्मानो दीना दुःखसमन्विताः। सत्येनातिपरीताङ्गा नोदीक्षन्ते स्म किञ्चन॥२२॥
verses.english: Looking at their countenance, the king Duryodhana with cheerful heart thus addressed the Suta, “O Pratikamin, bring her here. Let the Kurus give their answer before her presence."

verses.sanskrit: ततस्त्वेषां मुखमालोक्य राजा दुर्योधनः सूतमुवाच हृष्टः। इहैवैतामानय प्रातिकामिन् प्रत्यक्षमस्याः कुरवो ब्रुवन्तु॥२३॥
verses.english: Thereupon the Suta, ever obedient to his command and at the same time afraid of the anger of Drupada's daughter, giving up his pride, again spoke thus in the assembly, "What shall I say to Krishna (Draupadi)?

verses.sanskrit: ततः सूतस्तस्य वशानुगामी भीतश्च कोपाद्द्रुपदात्मजायाः। विहाय मानं पुनरेव सभ्यानुवाच कृष्णां किमहं ब्रवीमि॥२४॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Thereupon she, being (much) distressed, rose up in great affliction, and covering her pale face with her hands, ran to the place where were the ladies of the old king, the foremost of the Kurus (Dhritarashtra.)

verses.sanskrit: एह्येहि पाञ्चालि जितासि कृष्णे दुर्योधनं पश्य विमुक्तलज्जा। कुरून्भजस्वायतपत्रनेत्रे धर्मेण लब्धाऽसि सभां परैहि॥२४॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Thereupon she, being (much) distressed, rose up in great affliction, and covering her pale face with her hands, ran to the place where were the ladies of the old king, the foremost of the Kurus (Dhritarashtra.)

verses.sanskrit:
दूर्योधन उवाच।
              दुःशासनैष मम सूतपुत्रो वृकोदरादुद्विजतेऽल्पचेताः। स्वयं प्रगृह्यानय याज्ञसेनीं किं ते करिष्यन्त्यवशाः सपत्नाः॥२५॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having heard the command of his brother, that prince (Dushasana) rose with blood red eyes. Entering the house of those great carwarriors (the Pandavas), he thus spoke to the princess, Draupadi.
verses.bhavadeepa: मानं दुर्योधनस्याज्ञाभङ्गेन तस्य श्रेष्ठत्वं विहाय तिरस्कृत्य ॥२४॥

verses.sanskrit: ततः समुत्थाय स राजपुत्रः श्रुत्वा भ्रातुः शासनं रक्तदृष्टिः। प्रविश्य तद्वेश्म महारथानामित्यब्रवीद्द्रौपदीं राजपुत्रीम्॥२६॥
verses.english: Dushasana said O Panchali, O Krishna, come you have been won by us. Behold Duryodhana (now) casting aside your modesty. O lady of eyes like the wide lotus leaves, accept the Kurus as your lords. You have been virtuously won by us, therefore come to the Sabha.
verses.bhavadeepa: उद्विजते बिभेति । अवशाः अस्मद्दासत्वात् ॥२५॥

verses.sanskrit: ततः समुत्थाय सुदूर्मनाः सा विवर्णमामृज्य मुखं करेण। आर्ता प्रदुद्राव यतः स्त्रियस्ता वृद्धस्य राज्ञः कुरुपुङ्गवस्य॥२८॥
verses.english: Thereupon Dushasana, roaring in anger, ran after her and seized the queen (Draupadi) by her long, blue and wavy hair.
verses.bhavadeepa: मानं दुर्योधनस्याज्ञाभङ्गेन तस्य श्रेष्ठत्वं विहाय तिरस्कृत्य ॥२४॥

verses.sanskrit: ततो जवेनाभिससार रोषाद्दुःशासनस्तामभिगर्जमानः। दीर्घेषु नीलेष्वथ चोर्मिमत्सु जग्राह केशेषु नरेन्द्रपत्नीम्॥२९॥
verses.english: The hair that was (once) sprinkled with the water sanctified with Mantras in the great Rajasuya sacrifice were now forcibly seized by the son of Dhritarashtra who disregarded the prowess of the Pandavas.

verses.sanskrit: ये राजसूयावभृथे जलेन महाक्रतौ मन्त्रपूतेन सिक्ताः। ते पाण्डवानां परिभूय वीर्यं बलात्प्रमृष्टा धृतराष्ट्रजेन ॥३०॥
verses.english: Dragging the greatly long-haired Krishna (Draupadi) as if she was protectorless, although she had great protectors, Dushasana brought her into the Sabha trembling like the banian tree in a storm.
verses.bhavadeepa: ऊर्मिमत्सु वेणीरूपेण संनिवेशिततया च प्रवहन्नदीजलवन्निम्नोन्नतेषु । ऊर्मय वेण्यलङ्कारास्तद्वत्सु वा ॥२९॥

verses.sanskrit: स तां पराकृष्य सभासमीपमानीय कृष्णामतिदीर्घकेशीम्। दुःशासनो नाथवतीमनाथवच्चकर्ष वायुः कदलीमिवार्ताम्॥३१॥
verses.english: Having been thus dragged by him, she best her body down and spoke in a low voice “O wretch, O rude one, you should not take me before the assembly. I am in my season. I am attired only in one cloth."

verses.sanskrit: सा कृष्यमाणा नमिताङ्गयष्टिः शनैरुवाचाथ रजस्वलाऽस्मि। एकं च वासो मम मन्दबुद्धे सभां नेतुं नार्हसि मामनार्य॥३२॥
verses.english: While she was piteously praying to Krishna and Vishnu (Arjuna) who were Hari (Narayana) and Nara (on earth), he (Dushasana) dragged her forcibly by her black hair.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽब्रवीत्तां प्रसभं निगृह्य केशेषु कृष्णेषु तदा स कृष्णाम्। कृष्णं च जिष्णुं च हरिं नरं च त्राणाय विक्रोशति याज्ञसेनी॥३३॥
verses.english: Dushasana said O Yajnaseni, whether you are in your season, whether you are attired in one cloth, or whether you are naked, when you have been won (by us) at dice and made our slave, you are to live amongst our serving women as you best can.

verses.sanskrit:
दुःशासन उवाच।
              रजस्वला वा भव याज्ञसेनि एकाम्बरा वाप्यथवा विवस्त्रा। द्यूते जिता चासि कृताऽसि दासी दासीषु वासश्च यथोपजोषम्॥३४॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said With dishevelled hair and her attire half loosened on account of the cruel dragging of Dushasana, the modest Krishna (Draupadi), being consumed as it were by anger, thus spoke in a low voice.
verses.bhavadeepa: कृष्णजिष्णू हरिनरै नारायणनरावित्यर्थः ॥३३॥

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              प्रकीर्णकेशी पतितार्धवस्त्रा दुःशासनेन व्यवधूयमाना। ह्रीमत्यमर्षेण च दह्यमाना शनैरिदं वाक्यमुवाच कृष्णा॥३५॥
verses.english: Draupadi said All these persons in this assembly are men learned in all the Shastras, all devoted to the performances of sacrifices and other rites and all equal to Indra (in prowess). Some of them are my Gurus (superiors) and some who stand to me as such. I cannot stay before them in this state.
verses.bhavadeepa: यथोपजोषं यथारुचि ॥३४॥

verses.sanskrit: द्रौपद्युवाच। इमे समायामुपनीतशास्त्राः क्रियावन्तः सर्व एवेन्द्रकल्पाः। गुरुस्थाना गुरवश्चैव सर्वे तेषामग्रे नोत्सहे स्थातुमेवम्॥३६॥
verses.english: O Wretch, O man of cruel deeds, do not make me uncovered. Do not drag me in this way. The princes (the Pandavas) will not pardon you, even if the celestial with Indra become your allies.

verses.sanskrit: नृशंसकर्मंस्त्वमनार्यवृत मा मा विवस्त्रां कुरु मा विकार्षीः। न मर्षयेयुस्तव राजपुत्राः सेन्द्रापि देवा यदि ते सहायाः॥३७॥
verses.english: The high-souled of Dharma (Yudhisthira) is (now) bound by the obligation of the rules of morality. The ways of Dharma is subtle. Those only can ascertain them who son possess great clearness of vision. Forgetting his virtue, I am unwilling to admit even an atom of fault in my husband (Yudhisthira.)
verses.bhavadeepa: उपनीतशास्त्राः अध्यापितशास्त्राः । गुरुस्थानाः गुरुतुल्यस्थानाः पित्रादितुल्याः । एवम् एकवनत्वेन ॥३६॥

verses.sanskrit: इदं त्वकार्यं कुरुवीरमध्ये रजस्वलां यत्परिकर्षसे माम्। न चापि कश्चित्कुरुतेऽत्र कुत्सां ध्रुवं तवेदं मतमभ्युपेतः॥३९॥
verses.english: It is a most unworthy act that you are dragging me before these Kuru heroes, though I am in my season. But none rebukes you here; they are certainly of the same mind with you.

verses.sanskrit: धिगस्तु नष्टः खलु भारतानां धर्मस्तथा क्षत्रविदां च वृत्तम्। यत्र ह्यतीतां कुरु धर्मवेलां प्रेक्षन्ति सर्वे कुरवः सभायाम्॥४०॥
verses.english: O Fie! When all the Kurus in this assembly look silently on this act which transgresses the shore of the Kuru morality; the morality of the Bharatas have certainly been destroyed and the usage of those conversant with the Kshatriya practices have surely disappeared.
verses.bhavadeepa: कश्चिदपि तव कुत्सां न कुरुते किं तु सर्वोऽपि जनस्त्वदीयं मतमभ्युपेतः ॥३९॥

verses.sanskrit: द्रोणस्य भीष्मस्य च नास्ति सत्त्वं क्षत्तुस्तथैवास्य महात्मनोपि। राज्ञस्तथा हीममधर्ममुग्रं न लक्षयन्ति कुरुवृद्धमुख्याः॥४१॥
verses.english: Drona and Bhisma, Khattwa and also the king (Dhritarashtra) have lost their greatness, else why do these best of the Kuru elders look silently on this great crime.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              तथा ब्रुवन्ती करुणं सुमध्यमा भर्तॄन्कटाक्षैः कुपितानपश्यत्। सा पाण्डवान्कोपपरीतदेहान्सन्दीपयामास कटाक्षपातैः॥४२॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said The slender-waisted (Draupadi) thus cried in distress in that Sabha and cast a glance on her enraged husbands, the Pandavas, who were filled with fearful wrath. She inflamed them more by her that glance.
verses.bhavadeepa: अस्य राज्ञो धृतराष्ट्रस्य ॥४१॥

verses.sanskrit: हृतेन राज्येन तथा धनेन रत्नैश्च मुख्यैर्न तथा बभूव। यथा त्रपाकोपसमीरितेन कृष्णाकटाक्षेण बभूव दुःखम्॥४३॥
verses.english: They were not so much pained at the robbing of their kingdom, their wealth, and their costly gems, as they were by that glance of Krishna (Draupadi), full of modesty and anger.

verses.sanskrit: दुःशासनश्चापि समीक्ष्य कृष्णामवेक्षमाणां कृपणान्पतींस्तान्। आधूय वेगेन विसञ्ज्ञकल्पामुवाच दासीति हसन्सशब्दम्॥४४॥
verses.english: Seeing Krishna (Draupadi) looking at her helpless husbands, Dushasana dragged her more forcibly and repeatedly called her "slave" "slave," and he laughed aloud.

verses.sanskrit: कर्णस्तु तद्वाक्यमतीव हृष्टः सम्पूजयामास हसन्सशब्दम्। गान्धारराजः सुबलस्य पुत्रस्तथैव दुःशासनमभ्यनन्दत्॥४५॥
verses.english: At these words, Karna became vary glad and approved them by laughing aloud. The Gandhara king, the son of Subala (Shakuni), similarly applauded Dushasana.
verses.bhavadeepa: आधूय आकम्प्य ॥४४॥

verses.sanskrit: सभ्यास्तु ये तत्र बभूवुरन्ये ताभ्यामृते धार्तराष्ट्रेण चैव। तेषामभूद्दुः खमतीव कृष्णां दृष्ट्वा सभायां परिकृष्यमाणाम्॥४६॥
verses.english: Amongst all those that were present in the assembly, except these three and the son of Dhritarashtra (Duryodhana), every one was filled with great sorrow on seeing Krishna (Draupadi) thus dragged in the Sabha.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              न धर्मसौक्ष्म्यात्सुभगे विवेक्तुं शक्नोमि ते प्रश्नमिमं यथावत्। अस्वाम्यशक्तः पणितुं परस्वं स्त्रियाश्च भर्तुर्वशतां समीक्ष्य॥४७॥
verses.english: Bhisma said O blessed lady, knowing that one who has no wealth of his own cannot stake the wealth belonging to others and (knowing also) that wives are always at the command and disposals of their husbands, I am unable to decide properly the point put forward by you. The ways of morality is subtle.

verses.sanskrit: त्यजेत सर्वां पृथिवीं समृद्धां युधिष्ठिरो धर्ममथो न जह्यात्। उक्तं जितोऽस्मीति च पाण्डवेन तस्मान्न शक्नोमि विवेक्तुमेतत्॥४८॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira can abandon the whole world full of wealth, but he will never sacrifice morality. The Pandavas (Yudhisthira) himself has said, "I am won'. Therefore, I am unable to decide this matter.
verses.bhavadeepa: भर्तुर्वशतां दासभार्यापि दास्येवेति भावः ॥४७॥

verses.sanskrit: द्व्यूतेऽद्वितीयः शकुनिर्नरेषु कुन्तीसुतस्तेन निसृष्टकामः। न मन्यते तां निकृतिं युधिष्ठिरस्तस्मान्न ते प्रश्नमिमं ब्रवीमि॥४९॥
verses.english: Shakuni is matchless in dice. The son of Kunti has still willfully staked with him. The illustrious (Yudhisthira) does not consider that Shakuni played with him deceitfully. Therefore, I am unable to decide this matter.
verses.bhavadeepa: जितोऽस्मीति वदतात्मैन पराजितो न तु स्त्री ॥४८॥

verses.sanskrit: द्रौपद्युवाच। आहूय राजा कुशलैरनार्यैर्दुष्टात्मभिर्नैकृतिकैः सभायाम्। द्यूतप्रियैर्नातिकृतप्रयत्नः कस्मादयं नाम निसृष्टकामः॥५०॥
verses.english: Draupadi said The king (Yudhisthira) was summoned to this assembly, and through he does not possess any skill in dice, yet he was made to play with skillful, wicked, deceitful and desperate gamblers. How then can he be said to have staked voluntarily?
verses.bhavadeepa: न च राजजयेनैव त्वज्जयः सिद्ध्यति द्यूतमर्यादाविदा शकुनिनैव तव पृथक् पणीकरणादित्याह द्यूते इति । राजा तु पराज्ञया त्वां पणीकृतवान् न स्वेच्छयाऽतोऽस्वामी कथं पणितवानिति राज्ञोऽपि दोषो नास्ति । तथा च शकुनिबुद्ध्यैव त्वमजिता तच्च शकुनिर्न मन्यते इत्याह नेति यतः पणीकृता अतः प्रागजिता । यतश्चापरदासेन पणीकृता ततोऽप्यजितैवेति भावः ॥४९॥

verses.sanskrit: अशुद्धभावैर्निकृतिप्रवृत्तैरबुध्यमानः कुरुपाण्डवाग्र्यः। सम्भूय सर्वैश्च जितोऽपि यस्मात्पश्चादयं कैतवमभ्युपेतः॥५१॥
verses.english: The chief of the Kurus and the Pandavas was deprived of his senses by the wretches of deceitful conduct and unholy instincts acting in concert. He could not understand their tricks through vanquished, but he has now understood all.
verses.bhavadeepa: नातिकृतप्रयत्नोऽनभ्यस्तद्यूतः । राजा मां सभायामाहूय कथं निसृष्टकामः अनीशोऽपि सन् मदाह्वानेन शत्रून्सकामान्कथं कृतवानित्यर्थः ॥५०॥

verses.sanskrit: तिष्ठन्ति चेमे कुरवः सभायामीशाः सुतानां च तथा स्नुषाणाम्। समीक्ष्य सर्वे मम चापि वाक्यं विब्रूत मे प्रश्नमिमं यथावत्॥५२॥
verses.english: Here in this assembly are present the Kurus who are the lords of their sons and daughter-in-law. Let all of them, after duly reflecting on my words, properly answer me the question I have asked.
verses.bhavadeepa: जितोऽपीति । आत्मपराजयावसानत्वात् द्यूतस्य । कथं ततोऽप्युपरिदेवितवानित्यर्थः ॥५१॥

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              तथा ब्रुवन्तीं करुणं रुदन्तीमवेक्षमाणां कृपणान्पतींस्तान्। दुःशासनः परुषाण्यप्रियाणि वाक्यान्युवाचामधुराणि चैव॥५३॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Dushasana spoke many disagreeable and harsh words to Krishna (Draupadi) who was thus piteously weeping and bewailing and casting glances on her helpless husbands.
verses.bhavadeepa: विब्रूत विस्पष्टं ब्रूत न तु भोष्मवत्संदिग्धमिति भावः ॥५२॥

verses.sanskrit: तां कृष्यमाणां च रजस्वलां च स्रस्तोत्तरीयामतदर्हमाणाम्। वृकोदरः प्रेक्ष्य युधिष्ठिरं च चकार कोपं परमार्तरूपः॥५४॥
verses.english: Seeing her who was in her season thus dragged and her upper garments loosened, seeing her in that condition which she did not deserve, Vrikodara (Bhima), afflicted beyond endurance, cast his eyes on Yudhisthira and gave vest to his anger.
verses.bhavadeepa: तथेति भीष्मेण द्रौपदीमाहात्म्यख्यापनाय प्रश्नस्योत्तरं नोक्तम् । दुःशासनस्तु पाण्डवपक्षपातिनापि भीष्मेण संशयोपन्यासादस्माकमेव जय इति मन्वानो यत्किञ्चित्प्रललापेत्यर्थः॥५३॥
